brief_item.title: GPU中度非结构化稀疏矩阵推理加速
brief_item.direction_name: 芯片内存接口、数据搬移与软硬件协同
brief_item.core_conclusion: 针对GPU非结构化稀疏推理，三层存储格式协同利用稀疏张量核和CUDA核，在保持模型质量前提下提升吞吐并降低显存占用。
brief_item.mechanism: 三层格式提取2:4稀疏适配稀疏张量核，PDD编码处理剩余非零元，流水线重叠计算与访存。
brief_item.result: 50%稀疏度下端到端推理吞吐相比FlashLLM提升41.4%，显存峰值降低21.4%。
brief_item.boundary: 高稀疏度及prefill不及FlashLLM，缺HBM带宽与功耗实测。
brief_item.project_relevance: 验证内存层次与计算单元协同，专用格式实现计算访存重叠，需补功耗与带宽评估。

facts.title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices
facts.event_hint: DAC 2026 paper (63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference)
facts.problem: LLM inference cost is high. Pruning can reduce computation, but maintaining model quality limits pruning to moderate unstructured sparsity (~50%). At these sparsity levels, existing GPU sparse matrix multiplication (SpMM) kernels cannot outperform dense cuBLAS due to: (1) tensor core incompatibility with unstructured patterns, (2) high metadata overhead (~50% of storage at moderate sparsity), and (3) high on-chip decoding overhead that cannot be overlapped with HBM memory access.
facts.mechanism: Three-layer sparse matrix storage format with co-optimized SpMM kernel: (1) Sparse-TC layer extracts 2:4 structured sparsity patterns compatible with sparse tensor cores using 2-bit position metadata; (2) Slot-Filling layer handles surplus non-zeros (~17.7%) using Parallel Differential Distance (PDD) encoding (4-bit) for low-cost decoding; (3) Residual Layer (<1%) uses CSR format. The kernel jointly utilizes sparse tensor cores (for structured patterns) and CUDA cores (for PDD decoding and residual computation) with pipelined execution overlapping on-chip computation with global memory access.

evidence.claim: At 50% unstructured sparsity, LLM perplexity remains near dense levels (Wanda: 7.79 vs 5.47 for Llama-7B; RIA: 6.88 vs 5.47 on WikiText-2)
evidence.condition: 50% unstructured sparsity, Llama-7B, WikiText-2 dataset

evidence.claim: At 70% sparsity, perplexity degrades sharply (Wanda: 214.9, RIA: 68.8 vs 5.47 dense for Llama-7B)
evidence.condition: 70% unstructured sparsity, Llama-7B, WikiText-2 dataset

evidence.claim: At 50% sparsity, kernel achieves up to 1.64× speedup over SpInfer, 1.81× over FlashLLM, 5.29× over Sputnik
evidence.baseline: Sputnik (CUDA cores), SparTA, FlashLLM, SpInfer (tensor cores)
evidence.condition: 50% sparsity, OPT-30B/66B matrix shapes, batch sizes 16/32, H100 GPU

evidence.claim: End-to-end inference at 50% sparsity achieves 41.4% higher throughput than FlashLLM and 26.1% higher than SpInfer on OPT-30B with batch size 16
evidence.condition: OPT-30B, 50% sparsity, batch size 16, input/output sequence length 512, H100 SXM5 80GB HBM3

evidence.claim: Peak memory usage reduced by 21.4% compared to dense baseline at 50% sparsity on OPT-30B with batch size 16
evidence.condition: OPT-30B, 50% sparsity, batch size 16, H100 GPU

facts.evaluation_context: Target hardware: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPU with 80GB HBM3. Workload: OPT-30B and OPT-66B models pruned with Wanda algorithm. Batch sizes: 8, 16, 32. Sequence lengths: input 512, output 512. Sparsity levels: 50%, 60%, 70%. Baselines: cuBLAS_TC (dense tensor cores), SpInfer (EuroSys'25), FlashLLM (VLDB'24), Sputnik, SparTA. Evaluation covers both kernel-level SpMM and end-to-end LLM inference throughput (tokens/s) and memory usage.
facts.limitations: Evidence now covers complete evaluation including experimental setup (H100 SXM5 80GB HBM3), specific models (OPT-30B/66B with Wanda pruning), batch sizes (8/16/32), sequence lengths (512), and detailed throughput and memory results. However, HBM bandwidth utilization measurements, detailed memory traffic breakdown, and power consumption data remain unavailable. The method underperforms FlashLLM at high sparsity and during prefill phase with large N (compute-bound regime). No RIA pruning method evaluation found in supplement.
facts.project_relevance: This work is highly relevant to AI chip accelerator evaluation under the 'chip memory interface, data movement and hardware-software co-design' direction. It directly addresses how GPU memory hierarchy (HBM3), sparse tensor cores, and CUDA cores can be co-designed through specialized storage formats and kernel optimization to accelerate LLM inference at moderate sparsity. The focus on overlapping computation with HBM memory access, hierarchical memory strategy (L2 cache for dense matrices, global memory for sparse weights), and reducing metadata overhead aligns with project questions about memory bandwidth bottlenecks and hardware-software co-design. The supplement now provides comprehensive experimental validation with throughput improvements and memory reduction data.
source_notes: Evidence Pack: front-evidence-v2 (Sections 1-4.2) + targeted supplement (PDF Pages 5-6, Sections 5-7)
Authors: Tao Lu (NUS), Haoyu Wang (Zhejiang Univ), et al.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the detailed HBM bandwidth utilization, memory traffic breakdown, and power consumption measurements?

brief_item.title: KVCache分形归档压缩与索引
brief_item.direction_name: 压缩、增量传输、预取与放置
brief_item.core_conclusion: 分形归档格式通过低维向量序列化符号流，实现KVCache无损压缩并提供常数时间随机访问与子串检索能力。
brief_item.mechanism: 收缩迭代映射编码把符号序列转低维向量，提供O(1)随机访问与子串索引。
brief_item.result: 混合非对称RVQ实现36倍压缩（相对fp16），编码耗时每字符0.68微秒，随机访问耗时311微秒。
brief_item.boundary: 仅在GPT-2小模型验证，缺少跨域传输实测数据，码书训练依赖特定语料。
brief_item.project_relevance: 压缩比可降跨域KV传输字节，常数访问支持分布式缓存检索，需补生产规模验证。

facts.title: Fractal KV-Cache Archives: Lossless Symbolic Storage with In-Place Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Inference
facts.event_hint: arXiv publication on KV cache compression archive format
facts.problem: KV cache dominates memory cost of long-context autoregressive inference; once quantized to codebook indices, the resulting symbol stream needs storage that supports the access patterns of a growing cache (random access and append)
facts.mechanism: Contractive iterated-map code (fractal archive) that serializes symbol sequences into low-dimensional real vectors, providing lossless storage with O(1) random access and O(1) amortized append, while simultaneously functioning as a search index for approximate substring queries

evidence.claim: Codec encoding runs in linear time at 0.68µs per character
evidence.condition: on natural text, 25K-400K characters

evidence.claim: Random access costs 311µs per lookup
evidence.condition: 10^6-character document, decoding only the span containing the target

evidence.claim: Append operation costs 175µs per token (amortized)
evidence.condition: token-by-token append, re-walking only from last stored anchor

evidence.claim: Per-head hybrid bit-asymmetric RVQ (K×4, V×2) achieves 36x compression vs fp16 at +11.2% perplexity cost
evidence.condition: GPT-2 124M, 1024-token contexts, 4-sink + 32-recent exact window

evidence.claim: Archive-based search index achieves 1.00 recall for approximate substring queries
evidence.condition: Nearest-neighbor distance thresholding on stored vectors, query encoded from origin

facts.evaluation_context: GPT-2 (124M parameters) on The Time Machine (Project Gutenberg public domain text), 1024-token context windows, 4 attention sinks + 32 recent tokens kept exact, remainder archived. Perplexity measured token-by-token, baseline perplexity 35.97. Codebooks trained by k-means on disjoint span of same book. All experiments run on single laptop CPU within minutes. Code released at github.com/eighteight/fractal-kv.
facts.limitations: Evaluated only on GPT-2 (124M) - not validated on production-scale models. Archive format itself produces size comparable to bit-packing; compression ratio comes from upstream vector quantizer. Lossy regime (truncated points) forfeits random access and in-place search properties. Multi-span truncation damages recent context as much as distant context, requiring explicit exact-window policy rather than free recency gradient. Per-head codebooks trained per corpus rather than amortized - a deployable system would need corpus-independent or online codebooks. Serialization ties rather than beats byte-oriented coders on raw size; advantage is access pattern, not compression ratio. Study does not benchmark against concurrent random-access KV quantizers such as FibQuant.
facts.project_relevance: Directly addresses KV cache compression (36x vs fp16) which reduces transfer bytes for cross-region KV cache scenarios. Archive format's O(1) random access enables efficient retrieval patterns in distributed cache settings. Search index capability (1.00 recall) could enable content-based routing/prefetching across regions. Key/value asymmetry insight could inform selective compression strategies for transfer optimization. However, corpus-specific codebook training and lack of production-scale evaluation limit direct deployment readiness.
source_notes: Code and scripts released at https://github.com/eighteight/fractal-kv

evidence_gaps.question: What is the end-to-end bandwidth reduction and transfer time impact for cross-region KV cache deployment?
How does this approach scale to production-scale models (hundreds of kilobytes per token) and what are the consistency/maintenance overheads?

brief_item.title: LLM服务运行时模型并行重配置
brief_item.core_conclusion: ReMP将模型并行拓扑与运行时状态解耦，通过CPU共享内存持久化和二维KVCache迁移实现低停机在线重配置。
brief_item.mechanism: 拓扑状态解耦存权重于CPU共享内存，二维KV迁移在流水层与注意力头联合重映射。
brief_item.result: 7B至70B拓扑切换1至7秒，较重启快10至100倍，重叠执行省13%至32%转换时间。
brief_item.boundary: 缺少精确重启基准时间和详细通信开销，WAN传输开销未评估。
brief_item.project_relevance: 二维KV迁移为跨域状态重分布提供参考，状态与位置解耦适用于远程缓存，需评WAN时延。

facts.title: ReMP: Low-Downtime Runtime Model-Parallelism Reconfiguration for LLM Serving
facts.event_hint: arXiv paper on runtime reconfiguration of TP/PP topology for LLM serving
facts.problem: Existing LLM inference systems treat model parallelism topology (Tensor Parallelism TP and Pipeline Parallelism PP) as static configuration. This rigid design cannot adapt to dynamically changing inference workloads. State-of-the-art systems lack online reconfiguration capabilities and can only switch configurations by restarting the service, resulting in several minutes of service interruption, KV cache loss, and prohibitive recomputation overhead.
facts.mechanism: ReMP decouples model parallelism topology from runtime state through three key techniques: (1) Decoupling topology from state—persisting full model state in CPU shared memory, avoiding full service reconstruction; (2) Two-dimensional KV cache migration—jointly remapping cache blocks across pipeline layer dimension and tensor-parallel KV-head dimension to preserve reusable states; (3) End-to-end online reconfiguration integrated into vLLM v1 executor, worker management, KV cache manager, and communication pipeline. ReMP overlaps model-shard reloading with KV cache construction/migration during state-transformation since these operations work on different runtime states and data paths.

evidence.claim: ReMP topology switches complete within 1-7 seconds for models from 7B to 70B parameters, achieving speedups of tens to over 100× compared to restart-based reconfiguration
evidence.condition: Four LLMs evaluated: Llama2-7B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, Llama2-70B on H100 and RTX 5090 platforms (Llama2-70B excluded from RTX 5090 due to GPU memory limitations); exact baseline restart times not visible

evidence.claim: ReMP's overlap technique saves 13-32% of state-transformation time by executing model-shard reloading concurrently with KV cache construction or migration
evidence.baseline: sequential execution of model loading and KV transfer
evidence.condition: Overlap reduces optimized time toward max(T_model, T_KV) rather than sequential sum; savings measured across four models on both H100 and RTX 5090 platforms

evidence.claim: ReMP dynamically selects TP/PP configurations under varying request pressure using a weighted score combining output throughput (higher-is-better), mean TPOT (lower-is-better), and mean TTFT (lower-is-better)
evidence.value: dynamic topology selection with weighted score
evidence.condition: Evaluated across request rates 1-5 on four models using BurstGPT-derived request traces; selection metric balances capacity and user-visible latency

evidence.claim: ReMP consistently achieves lower TTFT and TPOT while delivering higher output throughput compared to fixed TP1PP8 and TP2PP4 baselines under medium and high request pressure
evidence.condition: Results consistent across H100 and RTX 5090 platforms; improvement most pronounced at higher request rates; exact numerical improvements not specified

evidence.claim: ReMP decouples four runtime states from launch-time topology: model weights, KV cache, communication groups, and workers
evidence.condition: Model weights reloaded via CPU memory, KV cache via 2D layer/head migration, comm groups via prebuilt snapshots, workers via standby/wakeup reuse

facts.evaluation_context: ReMP is integrated into vLLM v1 core modules. Experiments conducted on two 8-GPU platforms: NVIDIA H100 (AMD EPYC 7R13 CPU, 2TB memory) and NVIDIA RTX 5090 (Intel Xeon Gold 6530 CPU, 960GB memory) with four models ranging from 7B to 70B parameters (Llama2-7B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, Llama2-70B). Llama2-70B not evaluated on RTX 5090 due to GPU memory limitations. Serving performance evaluated using BurstGPT-derived request traces across request rates 1-5, comparing ReMP dynamic selection against fixed TP1PP8 and TP2PP4 baselines.
facts.limitations: Supplement covers Sections 4.1-4.3 including experimental setup details and serving performance under dynamic workload. Key gaps remain: exact baseline restart times for the 10-100× speedup claims are not specified; detailed workload parameters (input/output lengths, batch sizes) are not provided; communication overheads and data transfer volumes for KV cache migration are not quantified; exact numerical TTFT/TPOT/throughput improvements are shown qualitatively in figures but not specified in text. WAN/network transmission considerations are not addressed; paper focuses on intra-cluster GPU communication for TP/PP.
facts.project_relevance: ReMP's KV cache migration mechanism demonstrates state preservation across topology changes, which is relevant for cross-region KV cache migration. The two-dimensional remapping (layer + head) provides a design pattern for state redistribution. Overlap technique (13-32% time savings) shows concurrent state transformation potential. Dynamic topology selection methodology using weighted score (throughput, TPOT, TTFT) offers a framework for cross-region configuration decisions. However, ReMP operates in intra-cluster GPU context, not WAN. For cross-region scenarios, the WAN RTT/bandwidth costs must be weighed against migration benefits. ReMP's decoupling approach (separating logical state from physical placement) is applicable to remote cache design.
source_notes: Evidence pack is front-evidence-v2 strategy containing ~27% of full document
Supplement adds experimental setup (Section 4.1), switching time overlap analysis (Section 4.2, Figure 6), and dynamic workload serving performance (Section 4.3, Figures 7-8)
Four models now specified: Llama2-7B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, Llama2-70B
BurstGPT-derived request traces used for workload simulation
Hardware specifications now include CPU and host memory details

What are the communication overheads and data transfer volumes for KV cache migration during TP/PP topology switches?

brief_item.title: BlueField-4面向智能体AI工厂的随路卸载
brief_item.core_conclusion: BlueField-4通过嵌入式计算和内联加速卸载网络、存储、安全和遥测服务，STX存储处理器利用DOCA Memos管理KVCache上下文内存。
brief_item.mechanism: DPU集成800G网络与PCIe Gen6，DOCA Memos管KV Cache。
brief_item.result: 相比BlueField-3提供6倍算力、4倍内存容量和3倍内存带宽，STX支持1.6Tb/s以太网。
brief_item.boundary: 缺少CPU降低比例、端到端时延和吞吐实测数据，仅有架构能力描述。
brief_item.project_relevance: 展示网络、存储、安全与元数据随路卸载，DOCA Memos体现缓存与元数据卸载，需补量化评估。

facts.title: Scaling Agentic AI Factories Through Extreme Co-Design with NVIDIA BlueField
facts.event_hint: NVIDIA BlueField-4 and BlueField-4 STX announcement for agentic AI factories
facts.problem: Agentic AI transforms inference into a distributed workflow where infrastructure must move, protect, retrieve, and reuse context data (especially KV cache) at high speed without creating latency or consuming host CPU resources needed for agent execution
facts.mechanism: BlueField-4 DPU offloads networking, storage, security, telemetry, and control-plane services from host CPUs via embedded compute, inline acceleration, and DOCA software. BlueField-4 STX storage processor with DOCA Memos manages KV cache inline as active context-memory data path rather than passive storage tier.

evidence.claim: BlueField-4 integrates up to 800 Gb/s Ethernet or InfiniBand, 64-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, PCIe Gen6, and LPDDR5X memory
evidence.condition: BlueField-4 DPU maximum networking bandwidth

evidence.claim: BlueField-4 delivers up to 6x more compute performance, 4x memory capacity, and more than 3x memory bandwidth compared to BlueField-3
evidence.condition: Generational comparison claim; no specific workload or benchmark details provided

evidence.claim: BlueField-4 STX Storage Processor combines Vera CPU, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, up to 1.6 Tb/s Spectrum-X Ethernet connectivity
evidence.condition: BlueField-4 STX maximum Ethernet connectivity

evidence.claim: DOCA Memos enables KV cache management and sharing across compute and storage nodes for context reuse
evidence.condition: Qualitative capability claim; no performance metrics or validation data provided

evidence.claim: BlueField provides infrastructure processing across GPU compute, CPU execution, and AI-native storage layers in Vera Rubin platform
evidence.condition: Architectural integration claim; no quantitative deployment or performance data provided
evidence.source_locator: BlueField-4 across Vera Rubin AI factory section

facts.evaluation_context: The article describes a system architecture for agentic AI workloads on NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform with Rubin GPUs, Vera CPUs, NVLink scale-up, ConnectX-9/Spectrum-X scale-out networking, and CMX context memory storage platform. No specific workload, hardware configuration, or benchmark details are provided.
facts.limitations: No specific CPU reduction percentages, latency measurements, throughput numbers, deployment scale data, or validated end-to-end performance results. Claims are primarily qualitative architectural capability statements without supporting experimental data or quantified baselines.
facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to DPU inline datapath offload questions. BlueField-4 demonstrates comprehensive inline coverage of networking (HBN routing, ASTRA isolation), storage (KV I/O, metadata, data placement), security (zero-trust, policy enforcement), and telemetry services. However, article lacks quantitative evidence for卸载覆盖率, CPU下降比例, or 端到端时延. The DOCA Memos KV cache management is a concrete example of metadata/cache卸载组合.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the specific CPU utilization reduction percentages when BlueField-4 offloads networking, storage, and security services from host CPUs under agentic AI workloads?
What are the measured end-to-end latency improvements and throughput gains for agentic AI inference with BlueField-4 infrastructure offload compared to host-only processing?
What is the卸载覆盖率 for AI factory data path operations and what deployment scale has been validated in production?
